description: Rust-only migration reference for allowed adopted Full overlaps. Each rationale records the current ownership boundary; presence is not proof of behavioral parity. Disclosure markers retain compatibility warnings for older adopted providers.

overlaps.rationale: Both close through the engine; adopted callers use the serving owner projection, not an immediate edit to Electron sidebar state.
Both expose engine-backed agent snapshots; the serving owner applies its visibility/layout projection and the renderer can overlay local state.
Predicates observe the serving owner snapshots; desktop-only cached observations are not supplied to an adopted owner.
Orphan detection uses parent lineage known to the serving owner, not an assumed shared Electron in-memory registry.
Reparenting updates the serving owner lineage; this does not promise mutation of Electron local parent/wake caches.
Progress is delivered using the serving owner tracked parent identity and bounds; it cannot infer desktop-only lineage.
The serving owner submits messages to the same session engine and preserves acceptance versus queued acknowledgement.
The serving owner performs real engine admission and returns owned launch identity; per-provider launch controls are reviewed separately.
Rust uses its persistent headless analytics store; Electron has a separate session-history store. Current Rust is not the old all-zero/empty stub.
Rust computes persistent headless history/model totals; Electron history can include UI-owned history absent from that store. Current Rust does not return the old zero stub.
Returns the serving process cwd; per-process context is intentional and not a directory authorization grant.
Returns the serving host configured supervisor directory; actual filesystem behavior has owning handler tests.
Both modify the same selected brief using additive insertion, lock/CAS checks and selected-object containment.
Both preserve archive-first ordering and whole-line splicing under the same selected brief ownership contract.
Document parsing is shared, but liveness comes from the serving owner snapshots; desktop-only rows cannot be inferred.
Both forward an answer to the same engine-owned question endpoint, preserving session and request identity.
Both forward approval to the engine-owned prompt endpoint rather than maintaining independent permission state.
Both use the engine permission-gate operation; a UI local rendering layer is not the gate owner.
Both use the same handoff instruction, bounded file completion and fallback contract on the serving host.
Both use the engine handoff result with its markdown/path instead of fabricating a local completion.
The engine receives the effort operation; Electron local optimistic effort notes are a separate projection.
The owner distinguishes accepted versus queued model selection; desktop local optimistic cache behavior is not duplicated by the adopted owner.
Both use the provider/engine permission operation; Electron local optimistic metadata is distinct from authoritative engine acknowledgement.
Both signal the selected engine-owned process; no separate unmanaged process is selected by the overlapping method.
The legacy agent-facing V1 name retains its documented availability boundary; desktop.* workflow owner methods have separate contracts.

Rust performs header-only format/dimension probing and returns bounded original inline bytes; it has no image decoder/resizer. Electron can produce thumbnails and handle large eligible images differently, so the adopted-provider disclosure remains current.
Releases the serving owner path watch; it does not unwatch unrelated owners or widen ordinary filesystem authority.
Observes the selected path and emits fs.changed through the serving owner, including atomic replacement behavior.
Commits selected worktree changes with literal arguments and real Git error propagation. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads the selected commit diff through literal Git arguments and worktree operand containment. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads selected commit line statistics with the shared wire shape. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads selected worktree changes; pathspec and untracked operands remain bounded to that selected Git object. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads bounded Git history with the shared entry shape and argument contract. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads line statistics with literal arguments and UTF-8 path handling. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.

Discards one contained file's unstaged changes with literal Git arguments; a folder or path-less call is refused, never widened to the whole tree. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.

Fast-forwards the selected repository with literal Git arguments (no merge commit, no editor) and preserves its actual success/error acknowledgement. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Pushes through the selected repository Git operation and preserves its actual success/error acknowledgement. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Stages the caller selected paths using literal Git arguments, retaining empty-selection semantics. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Reads the selected repository status into the shared wire shape, including unusual filename characters. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Unstages the selected paths without converting malformed input into all-path scope. Ordinary host cwd access remains ambient; selected Git operands stay contained.
Full headless fallback logs instead of posting Electron in-app/OS notifications; default desktop hub-only composition deliberately leaves ownership to Electron.
The serving host resolves configured provider executables. Environment differences are explicit host observations, not a guessed remote installation.
The serving owner requests the selected provider catalog; unsupported/unavailable sources are not invented as launchable models.
The serving host executes bounded project search with the shared query/result contract; frontend matches must come from that selected filesystem.
Attaches the serving owner byte stream with caller-bound leases and replay; byte ownership stays with the engine.
Both read the same engine conversation; frontend retained-window and UI overlay behavior remains separately owned.
Releases only that caller terminal lease; other viewers retain their stream.
Rust now supplies owned persistent recents and metadata; Electron can have additional UI session history. Old peers with blank fields remain a compatibility concern.
Reads one engine-backed snapshot through the serving owner projection; it is not an Electron in-memory mutation.
Reads engine-backed snapshots through the serving owner projection and visibility filter.
Reads the provider-owned child conversation rather than inventing a top-level local session.
Forwards raw bytes or text without synthesized newline; typed root/field validation and byte precedence are tested on the real handler.
Renews only an existing lease belonging to the requesting connection.
Resizes the same owned PTY using validated dimensions; it does not create a new terminal.
Reads the engine/provider transcript through the serving owner path and shaping contract.
Creates an engine-owned headless PTY using the host login-shell policy and explicit cwd.
Rust publishes facade.openTerminal; Electron targets its renderer directly. Event acceptance does not guarantee an adopted Electron pane was displayed.
